Chicago, IL – September 25, 2026 – Stocks in this week's article are Match Group, Inc. MTCH, monday.com Ltd. MNDY, Ubiquiti Inc. UI and Semtech Corp. SMTC.
4 Top-Performing Liquid Stocks to Strengthen Your Portfolio
Liquidity measures a company's capability to meet short-term debt obligations. Stocks with high liquidity levels have always been in demand, owing to their potential to provide maximum returns. Investors seeking solid gains should add stocks with strong liquidity, which supports business growth.
Investors may want to consider adding four top-ranked stocks —Match Group, Inc., monday.com Ltd., Ubiquiti Inc. and Semtech Corp. — to their portfolios to boost returns.
However, one should be careful while investing in a stock with high liquidity levels. High liquidity may also indicate that the company cannot competently utilize its assets.
Besides sufficient cash, an investor might also consider a company's capital deployment abilities before investing. A balanced assessment of both liquidity and efficiency can help identify truly promising investment opportunities.
Current Ratio: It measures current assets relative to current liabilities. The ratio gauges a company's potential to meet short- and long-term debt obligations. A current ratio — the working capital ratio — below 1 indicates that the company has more liabilities than assets. A high current ratio does not always suggest that the company is in good financial shape. It may also indicate that the firm failed to utilize its assets significantly. Hence, a range of 1-3 is considered ideal.
Quick Ratio: Unlike the current ratio, the quick ratio — the "acid-test ratio" or "quick assets ratio" — indicates a company's ability to pay short-term obligations. It considers inventory, excluding current assets, relative to current liabilities. A quick ratio of more than 1 is desirable, like the current ratio.
Cash Ratio: This is the most conservative ratio among the three, considering cash, cash equivalents and invested funds relative to current liabilities. It measures a company's ability to meet existing debt obligations using the most liquid assets. Though a cash ratio of more than 1 may suggest sound financials, a higher number may indicate inefficiency in cash utilization.
A ratio greater than 1 is always desirable, but it may not always represent a company's financial condition.
Here are four of the 12 stocks that qualified the screen:
Match Group is the parent company of brands like Tinder, Hinge, Match, Meetic, OkCupid, Plenty Of Fish and more, helping people make meaningful connections. Dating app Tinder is the company's largest brand.
Hinge is a major growth contributor. Direct revenues for Hinge rose 22% year over year to $204 million in the second quarter of 2026. Adjusted EBITDA surged 48% to $79 million. Global MAU increased 13%, supported particularly by expansion markets. Overall, quarterly revenues of $853 million fell 1% year over year.
The company's potential growth driver is Tinder's product-led turnaround. On the last earnings call, management noted that updated recommendation algorithms have helped improve engagement, while Events could encourage new and lapsed users to reconsider Tinder. The company plans to expand Events from 10 cities currently to 26 cities by September and 75 cities by year-end.
For the third quarter, Match expects revenues of $885 million to $895 million, representing a year-over-year decline of 2% to 3%. The outlook includes a $10 million negative impact from Tinder user-experience tests and product changes, along with a $15 million negative impact from lower Azar revenues following its app redesign.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MTCH's 2026 earnings stands at $4.13 per share, unchanged in the past seven days. The company has a Growth Score of B.
monday.com specializes in the development of software applications. AI adoption is emerging as a big growth opportunity for the company. AI ARR doubled sequentially from the first quarter to the second quarter of 2026 and accounted for 17% of net new ARR added during the quarter. Second-quarter revenues of $364.6 million increased 22% year over year.
Customers generating more than $100,000 in ARR increased 37%, while those above $500,000 ARR jumped 68% year over year. Record net additions in both cohorts demonstrate that monday.com is successfully moving toward larger customers.
For the third quarter, monday.com expects revenues of $368-$370 million, implying 16%-17% year-over-year growth.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MNDY's 2026 earnings is $5.50 per share, unchanged over the past seven days. The company has a Growth Score of B and an average trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 23.56%.
Ubiquiti, along with its subsidiaries, offers networking products and solutions for service providers, enterprises and smart homes. Its service-provider platforms provide infrastructure for fixed wireless broadband, wireless backhaul and routing, while enterprise platforms include wireless local area network infrastructure, video surveillance, switching and routing solutions, security gateways and door access systems.
Fiscal 2026 revenues rose 27.2% to $3.27 billion as both webstore and distributor sales increased. No customer represented 10% or more of fiscal 2026 revenues, limiting dependence on any single buyer.
Enterprise Technology remains Ubiquiti's primary growth engine, supported by integrated networking and IT management offerings. Fiscal 2026 Enterprise Technology revenues rose 32% to $2.97 billion and increased to 91% of total revenues from 88% in fiscal 2025.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $17.08 per share, unchanged over the past seven days. The company has a Growth Score of B and an average trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 31.86%.
Semtech manufactures high-performance semiconductor chips for AI data center networking and connected IoT devices.
The company is benefiting from strong data-center demand, particularly across its FiberEdge, CopperEdge and emerging photonics portfolio. The company's photonics portfolio includes semiconductor optical amplifiers, high-power lasers and high-speed photodiodes for scale-up, scale-out and scale-across data center connectivity applications.
Data-center revenues reached $100 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 39% sequentially and 91% year over year. The top line was supported by continued strength in 800G products and a ramp in 1.6T CopperEdge and the ramp of 1.6T FiberEdge. LoRa represents another major growth engine.
LoRa-enabled net sales increased 31% sequentially and 58% year over year to $58 million. Growing traction for the LoRa Gen 4 platform, including LoRa Plus and other RF protocols, bodes well. For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Semtech expects net sales to be $410 million (+/- $5 million).
The company recently integrated its AirLink secure edge 5G/LTE routers and network management portfolio with Palo Alto Networks' Next-Generation Firewalls to deliver automated, edge-to-core safety for critical infrastructure operators and utilities.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMTC's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $3.48 per share, unchanged in the past seven days. The company has a Growth Score of A and an average trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 9.82%.

Rivet launches nationwide introducing a new approach to dating: Social Matching
Founded by former Tinder and Match Group exec Taru Kapoor, Rivet brings people and community back into dating
NEW YORK, Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rivet, a new dating network, today launches nationwide across the United States. Founded by former Tinder and Match Group executive Taru Kapoor, Rivet introduces Social Matching, a model that lets people help each other find meaningful connections and love.
Rivet's Social Matching harnesses the collective intuition of people with different perspectives to surface introductions that people might swipe past on conventional dating apps. The company has raised $10.5 million in seed funding, backed by Peak XV Partners, Shine Capital and Blume Ventures, to build and scale their innovative people-powered approach to dating.
Users can join Rivet not just to find connections for themselves but also to help others find love. As a Matcher, one weighs in on potential pairs and recommends introductions one thinks could work. The pairs who get high Social Matching scores are introduced to each other, and each individual independently decides whether they want to match with someone and begin a conversation. Rivet is for everyone, even if you're not currently dating, you can join as a Matcher and can help someone else find love and meaningful connections.
In a national survey of 2,013 U.S. adults commissioned by Rivet*, more than two-thirds (68%) of Gen Z and Millennials surveyed said they would be interested in helping someone they don't personally know find a potential romantic match, if they could do so anonymously and the person made the final decision, including 78% of Gen Z and 60% of Millennials. When asked what would make them interested in helping someone else find a romantic match, the top motivations were helping someone find love (36%) and helping someone avoid a bad match (27%).
"Dating has always been social," said Taru Kapoor, Founder and CEO of Rivet. "I spent many years thinking what we were building was removing friction from meeting people. Instead, we removed the people. Online dating apps created millions of connections in the last decade, mostly because they expanded the pool, connecting people to those they wouldn't have met otherwise. A huge side effect of that was that they turned something as fundamentally social and human as dating into a lonely, overwhelming activity which felt transactional and isolating.
I built Rivet to change that. Rivet is built on a simple truth: humans understand chemistry and compatibility in a way that no algorithm can. You don't have to find your person entirely on your own, let people help you find your person."
Rivet's model is built around a give-to-get philosophy as Matchers help each other find meaningful connections, creating a community where people can play an active role in each other's love stories. "Social matching takes the best of human intuition and judgment and uses it to bring people together. It's not a feature, it's the entire point of the platform. Matchers win when two people actually match, which is what single daters want instead of endless swiping. It's win-win," said Kapoor.
Elie Seidman, former CEO of Tinder and OkCupid, and an early investor in Rivet, who advised and mentored Kapoor throughout Rivet's development, said, "The swipe was one of the defining product innovations in online dating because it changed the fundamental way people discovered each other. For the first time since the swipe, the category has something genuinely new: human judgment and a real social community built on the foundation of state-of-the-art technology, working at scale. That is what turns a dating app into a dating network, and it is a powerful, category defining shift."
Rivet is free to download on iOS and Android.
Founded in 2025 by Taru Kapoor, who spent nearly a decade building and scaling Tinder and other Match Group brands across the U.S., Europe and Asia, Rivet is a Social Matching and dating network built around the belief that human intuition can recognize chemistry in ways algorithms cannot. Rivet's Social Matching model brings community into the dating experience, with Matchers vibe-checking potential pairs before introducing matches. The individual always makes the final decision on whether to view and match with an Introduction. Anyone can join Rivet purely as a Matcher to help people find their person. Rivet launched nationally in the U.S. in September 2026 and is a product of MeantToBe, Inc., based in New York. Learn more at rivetdating.com, and connect with the brand on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and LinkedIn.
Note:
**Research was conducted by Censuswide among 2,013 US nationally representative general consumers between 15.09.2026-18.09.2026. Censuswide is a member of the Market Research Society and the British Polling Council, and a signatory of the Global Data Quality Pledge.

Match CEO: AI chatbot relationships could worsen the loneliness epidemic
Match Group (MTCH) CEO Spencer Rascoff is hoping a product revamp at Tinder could do its part in addressing the loneliness epidemic — which may only get worse because of AI companions.
"There is a loneliness epidemic. It is existential for our species. It is a mental health crisis that comes from that loneliness," Rascoff told Yahoo Finance from the Goldman Sachs Communacopia & Tech Conference (video above). "Most of the other technology companies out there … are about increasing engagement. We are about creating human connection. And so I really think that this is why I came out of retirement to take this job as CEO of Match Group. I connected deeply with this mission. I think we're one of the very few companies that can make a dent in the loneliness epidemic."
Rascoff has pushed the company into live events for people to meet, with more on the way.
He has also improved Tinder's user experience to focus more on quality engagement, bringing the company to the cusp of delivering daily active user growth after many quarters of decline.
"That's dystopian [the relationships with AI chatbots] and we stand against it," Rascoff said. "And I think just as social media made people's connection with one another worse. I mean, it's called social media, but it's not even really that social anymore. It's not about connecting with your friends. It's more about consuming content of creators. I think AI has the potential to make this loneliness epidemic even worse as people start to form relationships or pseudo-relationships — what they perceive to be relationships — with AI. And we are the human connection company. We think humans need humans now more than ever, and we can help create that."
The turnaround has only started to take shape, Rascoff noted.
Match Group reported mixed second quarter financial results, with sales up 1% from the prior year.
Despite top-line friction from user declines at Tinder, the company's bottom-line performance proved more resilient. Match posted a 14% rise in adjusted operating profits.
The continued subscriber pressure at Tinder outweighed Hinge's (HNGE) strong 22% growth.
Match stock is up 26% year to date.
Match rival Bumble's (BMBL) stock is down 19% on the year as the company deals with its own set of pressured results.
"We think new product experiences (in real life events, video speed dating) and marketing will help here (as will positive word-of-mouth) though category/cultural backdrop should remain a significant challenge," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney said.

4 Top-Performing Liquid Stocks to Strengthen Your Portfolio
Liquidity measures a company's capability to meet short-term debt obligations. Stocks with high liquidity levels have always been in demand, owing to their potential to provide maximum returns. Investors seeking solid gains should add stocks with strong liquidity, which supports business growth.
Investors may want to consider adding four top-ranked stocks —Match Group, Inc., monday.com Ltd., Ubiquiti Inc. and Semtech Corp. — to their portfolios to boost returns.
However, one should be careful while investing in a stock with high liquidity levels. High liquidity may also indicate that the company cannot competently utilize its assets.
Besides sufficient cash, an investor might also consider a company's capital deployment abilities before investing. A balanced assessment of both liquidity and efficiency can help identify truly promising investment opportunities.
Current Ratio: It measures current assets relative to current liabilities. The ratio gauges a company's potential to meet short- and long-term debt obligations. A current ratio — the working capital ratio — below 1 indicates that the company has more liabilities than assets. A high current ratio does not always suggest that the company is in good financial shape. It may also indicate that the firm failed to utilize its assets significantly. Hence, a range of 1-3 is considered ideal.
Quick Ratio: Unlike the current ratio, the quick ratio — the "acid-test ratio" or "quick assets ratio" — indicates a company's ability to pay short-term obligations. It considers inventory, excluding current assets, relative to current liabilities. A quick ratio of more than 1 is desirable, like the current ratio.
Cash Ratio: This is the most conservative ratio among the three, considering cash, cash equivalents and invested funds relative to current liabilities. It measures a company's ability to meet existing debt obligations using the most liquid assets. Though a cash ratio of more than 1 may suggest sound financials, a higher number may indicate inefficiency in cash utilization.
A ratio greater than 1 is always desirable, but it may not always represent a company's financial condition.

Rivet launches nationwide introducing a new approach to dating: Social Matching
Founded by former Tinder and Match Group exec Taru Kapoor, Rivet brings people and community back into dating
NEW YORK, Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rivet, a new dating network, today launches nationwide across the United States. Founded by former Tinder and Match Group executive Taru Kapoor, Rivet introduces Social Matching, a model that lets people help each other find meaningful connections and love.
Rivet's Social Matching harnesses the collective intuition of people with different perspectives to surface introductions that people might swipe past on conventional dating apps. The company has raised $10.5 million in seed funding, backed by Peak XV Partners, Shine Capital and Blume Ventures, to build and scale their innovative people-powered approach to dating.
Users can join Rivet not just to find connections for themselves but also to help others find love. As a Matcher, one weighs in on potential pairs and recommends introductions one thinks could work. The pairs who get high Social Matching scores are introduced to each other, and each individual independently decides whether they want to match with someone and begin a conversation. Rivet is for everyone, even if you're not currently dating, you can join as a Matcher and can help someone else find love and meaningful connections.
In a national survey of 2,013 U.S. adults commissioned by Rivet*, more than two-thirds (68%) of Gen Z and Millennials surveyed said they would be interested in helping someone they don't personally know find a potential romantic match, if they could do so anonymously and the person made the final decision, including 78% of Gen Z and 60% of Millennials. When asked what would make them interested in helping someone else find a romantic match, the top motivations were helping someone find love (36%) and helping someone avoid a bad match (27%).
"Dating has always been social," said Taru Kapoor, Founder and CEO of Rivet. "I spent many years thinking what we were building was removing friction from meeting people. Instead, we removed the people. Online dating apps created millions of connections in the last decade, mostly because they expanded the pool, connecting people to those they wouldn't have met otherwise. A huge side effect of that was that they turned something as fundamentally social and human as dating into a lonely, overwhelming activity which felt transactional and isolating.
I built Rivet to change that. Rivet is built on a simple truth: humans understand chemistry and compatibility in a way that no algorithm can. You don't have to find your person entirely on your own, let people help you find your person."
Rivet's model is built around a give-to-get philosophy as Matchers help each other find meaningful connections, creating a community where people can play an active role in each other's love stories. "Social matching takes the best of human intuition and judgment and uses it to bring people together. It's not a feature, it's the entire point of the platform. Matchers win when two people actually match, which is what single daters want instead of endless swiping. It's win-win," said Kapoor.
Elie Seidman, former CEO of Tinder and OkCupid, and an early investor in Rivet, who advised and mentored Kapoor throughout Rivet's development, said, "The swipe was one of the defining product innovations in online dating because it changed the fundamental way people discovered each other. For the first time since the swipe, the category has something genuinely new: human judgment and a real social community built on the foundation of state-of-the-art technology, working at scale. That is what turns a dating app into a dating network, and it is a powerful, category defining shift."
Rivet is free to download on iOS and Android.

The individual always makes the final decision on whether to view and match with an Introduction. Anyone can join Rivet purely as a Matcher to help people find their person. Rivet launched nationally in the U.S. in September 2026 and is a product of MeantToBe, Inc., based in New York. Match CEO: AI chatbot relationships could worsen the loneliness epidemic
Match Group (MTCH) CEO Spencer Rascoff is hoping a product revamp at Tinder could do its part in addressing the loneliness epidemic — which may only get worse because of AI companions.
"There is a loneliness epidemic. It is existential for our species. It is a mental health crisis that comes from that loneliness," Rascoff told Yahoo Finance from the Goldman Sachs Communacopia & Tech Conference (video above). "Most of the other technology companies out there … are about increasing engagement. We are about creating human connection. And so I really think that this is why I came out of retirement to take this job as CEO of Match Group. I connected deeply with this mission. I think we're one of the very few companies that can make a dent in the loneliness epidemic."
Rascoff has pushed the company into live events for people to meet, with more on the way.
He has also improved Tinder's user experience to focus more on quality engagement, bringing the company to the cusp of delivering daily active user growth after many quarters of decline.
"That's dystopian [the relationships with AI chatbots] and we stand against it," Rascoff said. "And I think just as social media made people's connection with one another worse.
